topic.name: Properties of Transformed Square Root Functions

question.text:
Let $f(x)=a\sqrt{x+b}+c.$ Now consider the following properties of $f(x)\mathbin{:}$

  • The domain of $f(x)$ is $x\in \left[1, \infty\right).$

  • The range is $f(x)\in [2, \infty).$

  • The point $(5, 4)$ lies on the graph of $y=f(x).$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
question.explanation:
Let's consider each property in turn.

  • The domain of $f(x)=a\sqrt{x+b}+c\,$ is determined by the following inequality: \begin{align*} x+b &\ge 0 \\[3pt] x &\ge -b \end{align*} We are given that the domain is $x\in \left[1, \infty\right),$ which is equivalent to $x\ge 1.$ Hence, we obtain \[ -b=1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad b=-1. \]

  • Since the range is unbounded on the right-hand side, we know that $a>0.$ Furthermore, since we are given that the lowest point in the range is $2,$ we must have \begin{align*} \underbrace{a\sqrt{x-1}}_{\geq 0}+c \ge 2. \end{align*} This means that $c=2.$

  • Finally, since the point $(5,4)$ lies on the graph of $y=f(x),$ we have \begin{align*} f(5) &=a\sqrt{5-1}+2 \\[3pt] 4 &=2a + 2 \\[3pt] 2a&=2 \\[3pt] a&=1. \end{align*}

Therefore, our function is $f(x)=\sqrt{x-1}+2$ and

\[ a+b+c = 1 + (-1) + 2 = 2. \]

example.title: Finding a Transformed Square Root Function Given Some Properties

question.explanation:
To find the root of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0\mathbin{:}$ \[ \sqrt{3x+1} - 2 = 0 \]

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

\begin{align*} \sqrt{3x+1} - 2 & = 0 \\[3pt] \sqrt{3x+1} & = 2 \\[3pt] \big(\sqrt{3x+1}\big)^2 & = 2^2 \\[3pt] 3x+1 & = 4 \\[3pt] 3x & = 3 \\[3pt] x & = 1 \end{align*}

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

\begin{align*} \sqrt{3 \cdot 1+1} - 2 & = 0 \\[3pt] \sqrt{4} & = 2 \\[3pt] 2 &= 2 \quad {\color{green}\checkmark} \end{align*}

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=1.$

example.title: Finding the Roots of a Transformed Square Root Function

question.explanation:
To find the root of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0\mathbin{:}$ \[ 3\sqrt{1-x} + 2 = 0 \]

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

\begin{align*} 3\sqrt{1-x} + 2 & = 0 \\[3pt] 3\sqrt{1-x} & = -2\\[3pt] \sqrt{1-x} & = -\dfrac23\\[3pt] \end{align*}

This equation does not have any solutions since its left-hand side is always nonnegative, while the right-hand side is negative.

Therefore, $f(x)$ has no roots.
